All three files are in the outbox corrected, since anything I only argue for gets wiped with the round.

**House rule 1.** The mark itself is absent from all three sections, as Priya verified, but the rule was supposed to be a *plot point* and it was only a character trait. Prue now closes it in the preface in her own register: "Mark's manuscript contains four thousand and ten em-dashes. This edition contains none. That is the one place where I overruled him, and I did not ask." Twenty-six words against the twenty-nine Priya counted the preface short. It also produces a rhyme neither half points at: she removes the marks without asking, the spellcheck joins his name without asking. I asked for approval last round and nobody answered, so I made the call; refuse it and both sentences come out with nothing else moved.

**Seam fault, mine.** Chapter one had him write down the page "which he would have reason to look at again later, in front of somebody else." That's the narrator teasing a scene two chapters ahead, which is exactly what the room banned in the preface. Cut, and the chapter two payoff still works off a twenty-month-old page number.

**Repeated beats, mine.** Four "for a while"s across three sections, two gone. Four trailing "which" clauses carrying the joke, one gone.

**One soft number gone.** "Forty thousand deposits" was rhetorical scale in a book where every other number is checkable. The archive now tells Prue when a page was written and by whom, and never once what it was for.

**Priya's** outstanding half-line is paid outright: "I went on wanting it for years after I had read them properly."
